stories.title: Cyberattacks hit Russia, Ukraine emergency warning apps
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine have both said their emergency warning apps have been hit by apparent cyberattacks. Russia said its app came under a "massive cyberattack" this morning, hours after Ukraine reported a hack in an apparent exchange of blows between the foes, as their longest truce came to an end. The Kremlin's emergencies ministry said hackers posted "false information" on the app, which is designed to warn the public of incoming drone attacks and other threats. Hours earlier, Ukraine said it suspected its air raid alert system had been compromised, after baseless alerts of a radiation threat appeared on the app. The cyberattacks came as the longest truce of the war, limited to Ukraine's eastern Kherson region, ended yesterday after Russia refused the offer of an extension, according to Kyiv. Moscow did not immediately say who was behind the attack on its app, while Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications SPRAVDI blamed the hack it suffered on Russia.

stories.title: Ryanair's half year profit falls 15% as fuel costs rise
stories.summary: Ryanair is reviewing all its costs due to higher fuel prices and may require staff to take temporary pay freezes, the low-cost airline said today after reporting a 15% decline in net profit for the six months to the end of September. Ryanair is Europe's largest airline in terms of passenger numbers. It said that while it expects short-haul airfares to rise materially next year, that is unlikely to fully offset an estimated €2 billion increase in its fuel bill for the financial year that ends in March 2028, based on current forward prices. "Unless there is a swift resolution of the Middle East conflict, we expect jet fuel prices to remain elevated well into 2027," group chief executive Michael O'Leary said in a statement. Mr O'Leary added that negotiations with airports, lower crewing ratios and increased use of AI in back-office operations could also yield cost savings. Ryanair said its average fares fell by 4% year-on-year in the the first half of it fiscal year to €55.70 from €58 and are trending modestly ahead of the same period a year earlier in the current quarter.

stories.title: O'Connell wants focus to move on after Furlong fallout
stories.summary: Andy Farrell will be hoping to draw a line through the fallout of Tadhg Furlong's citing last week, but the discourse surrounding the incident looks likely to put a spotlight on how Ireland's players are approaching the ruck this month. Furlong had been cited after an allegation that he had grabbed the testicles of Munster's Gavin Coombes during their BKT United Rugby Championship Interpro just over a week ago. Footage showed the Leinster tighthead prop attempting to clear Coombes at a breakdown by putting an arm under his legs and lifting him off the ball. However, with no clear footage of Furlong attempting to target the testicles of the Munster player, he was unanimously cleared of wrongdoing by an independent disciplinary committee, which added that Coombes had given "an honest account of his recollection of events surrounding the incident." As expected, news of an Irish player escaping a suspension before an international break didn't escape the attention of Rassie Erasmus, whose incendiary social media posts on Friday have now unleashed the fury of thousands of South African keyboard warriors on Irish rugby, three weeks out from a meeting between the two sides. Erasmus will no doubt play dumb. By not directly referencing the Furlong citing, there might be just enough plausible deniability to wriggle away from trouble, even if all 230,000 of his followers on X knew what he was talking about.

stories.title: Ash shirt collaboration attracts fans around the world
stories.summary: Fans of the band Ash from across the world have sold out a Northern Ireland football team's special collaboration shirt with the threesome. The Ash x Ards FC collab marks the 30th anniversary of the group’s debut album 1977, recreating the original album cover in black, green and white. Lead singer Tim Wheeler also suggested the number 77 be put on the back of the shirt for which a third run is currently being planned to cope with demand from Taiwan, Japan and Australia as well as the United States. Although the band originally hails from Downpatrick, drummer Rick McMurray attended Ards FC matches in his youth with his father. The collab was announced with a video on social media last Monday featuring McMurray and Wheeler, along with Mark Hamilton wearing the shirts. McMurray says from the age of three his father took him to see Ards FC play every weekend, adding: "Now look at us, we have Ards FC football shirts, 1977 based, ain’t they pretty?".

stories.title: Miriam O'Callaghan: "I feel like I've won the lotto"
stories.summary: With no intention of slowing down, Miriam O'Callaghan is adding a new documentary to her busy work schedule. In the two-part show, Ireland’s Population Crash, the veteran broadcaster takes a look at the forces creating the country’s birth rate decline. She talks to Janice Butler about gratitude for her own children, her can-do attitude, and being a force for women in the workplace. "I had something on earlier," she explains why she’s dressed up. "I’m busy, always busy," she laughs. While she may have had something on, Miriam always looks well, part of her brand and general outlook on life: if she looks well, she feels well. It’s something she wrote about in her memoir, Life, Work, Everything, published last year. "I like to look well for myself. I love clothes and glamour. And why not? You can be glamorous and intelligent – they’re not mutually exclusive, as we now know," she laughs. Being in her 60s, she’s regularly asked about retirement, but she’s going nowhere. In fact, she’s as busy as ever with Prime Time, her weekend radio show and now a new documentary, Ireland’s Population Crash, a two-parter that explores the forces behind collapsing birth rates and shifting demographics that are quietly transforming the Ireland we thought we knew. "I totally respect people who want to retire. I don’t even like the thought of it; the idea of it is like retiring from life," she laughs. "There are 24 hours in every day, and I live life to the full, always have, always will. I find every day exciting. I’d say I’m very annoying to live with – they don’t say I am, but I’m sure I am."

stories.title: Public sector unions to meet over possible strike action
stories.summary: Public sector trade unions will meet today to discuss possible strike action on Wednesday 11 November over delays in agreeing a new pay deal. Talks on an agreement were adjourned on Friday night with unions claiming the process had reached a "significant impasse". The Workplace Relations Commission (WRC) has requested that a Government-appointed group assist in the stalled pay talks. Unions are expected to meet the group tomorrow but before that they will gather today to consider proposals for a strike on Wednesday week, which would include a major demonstration in Dublin and other rallies in regional locations. Over the weekend, Minister for Public Expenditure and Reform Jack Chambers expressed disappointment that despite intensive negotiations over 10 days, the public service pay discussions have not yet delivered an agreed outcome. Mr Chambers said that he recognised the efforts of all parties over recent weeks and thanked the WRC for its role in supporting the discussions.

stories.title: Who does the 'wife-work' in your workplace?
stories.summary: Analysis: Much of the knowledge that helps a workplace function is held by people who understand its systems, history and, importantly, one another We often talk about the importance of collegiality and care in our workplaces, but how much attention do we pay to the people, time and effort that make them possible? Much of what makes a workplace function well happens in the spaces between formal responsibilities. A colleague takes time to explain an unfamiliar process. Someone notices that a member of the team is having a difficult week and reaches out. An experienced employee helps resolve a problem before it develops into something more serious. These contributions may seem ordinary and often go unnoticed but they can profoundly shape how people experience work and how effectively an organisation operates.The Irish saying 'ar scáth a chéile a mhaireann na daoine', referenced recently in Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers' Budget 2027 speech, is often translated as "we live in the shelter of one another", yet scáth also means shadow. That double meaning captures an important tension about workpladce life. We benefit from the shelter provided by our colleagues, often without seeing the work involved in creating it or the shadow it may cast over their own working lives or professional trajectory. In my research on occupational wellbeing, I have found that universities are particularly dependent on this kind of contribution. Teaching, research and professional services rely on relationships and cooperation that cannot always be prescribed in policies or captured in workload models. Much of the knowledge that helps an institution function is held by people who understand its systems, its history and, importantly, one another. They know when a colleague needs support, whom to contact when something goes wrong and how to navigate situations that do not fit neatly into established procedures. This is sometimes described as relational labour, but very few of us would use that expression in everyday conversation. We are more likely to call it being helpful or being supportive. These are qualities we value in others and, hopefully, we try to practise ourselves. However, there is a difference between valuing collegiality and depending on it without giving due regard to what it requires.

stories.title: Nations League could offer Ireland ticket to the LA Games
stories.summary: The draw for the 2027 UEFA Women's Nations League takes place at midday on Tuesday, and it could be the start of the Republic of Ireland's journey to the LA Olympic Games. Carla Ward's side will take on Poland in a two-legged World Cup play-off final in December having breezed past Kazakhstan last month. The Girls in Green travel to Gdansk on Tuesday 1 December, before hosting the return game at Aviva Stadium four days later. Ireland were excellent in League A of World Cup qualifying, beating the Poles twice and the Netherlands in Cork to finish third in the the group. That means the Girls in Green will be in League A of the next Nations League, which begins in February. League A features Europe's top 16 countries divided into four seeded pots of four teams. If they were to win their four-team group, they would progress to the semi-final stage of the Nations League Finals, and therefore achieve a historic qualification for the 2028 Olympics. The women's Olympics soccer tournament has been expanded to 16 teams, with four European spots up for grabs. While the men's competition is primarily for Under-23s (each country is allowed just three overage players), there is no age limit for the women's event. England are the team nominated to represent Team Great Britain. Scotland and Wales (both in Pot 4) cannot be drawn into the same group as the Lionesses (Pot 2).

stories.title: Klum transforms into bloodied hand for Halloween bash
stories.summary: Heidi Klum underwent a bloody transformation to become a giant, gruesome severed hand for her annual Halloween party in New York on Saturday. German-American model Klum, famed for her extravagant Halloween costumes, looked unrecognisable as she transformed into a severed human hand. The star shared several photos posed up as the bloodied limb, accompanied by a series of hand-based puns, ahead of the party, 25 years after she began hosting the event. Zendaya, Cara Delevingne, Kourtney Kardashian, Neil Patrick Harris and his husband David Burtka were among other celebrities getting in the Halloween spirit over the weekend. Harris and Burtka were dressed as the twins from The Shining. Actress Zendaya wowed as she dressed as Halle Berry, recreating the star's look from the New York premiere of X-Men in 2000.

stories.title: Report on how Covid-19 was handled due at end of year
stories.summary: The independent review into how Ireland handled the Covid-19 pandemic has said it is on track to deliver its final report by the end of the year. In recent months, the COVID-19 Evaluation has met with key people who were involved in dealing with the pandemic, including: Taoiseach Micheál Martin; former taoiseach Leo Varadkar; the former Chief Medical Officer Dr Tony Holohan; and key members of the National Public Health Emergency Team (NPHET). The independent Evaluation will hold a live-streamed debate this morning with experts to discuss how future national emergencies should be managed. The proceedings will run from 10am to 12.45pm and can be viewed on the Evaluation's website, covid19evaluation.ie, and on its YouTube channel. The proceedings will include: Dr Caroline McMullan, Architect of the National Risk Assessment for Ireland; Lucy Easthope, Professor in Practice of Risk and Hazard, University of Durham; and Professor Pete Lunn, Head of the ESRI Behavioural Research Unit. The evaluation was set up by the Government in late 2024, and is a non-statutory review, chaired by Professor Anne Scott, assisted by an evaluation team of experts.

stories.title: Manufacturing activity grows strongly in October - PMI
stories.summary: The manufacturing sector expanded strongly in October, supported by sharp rises in output and new orders and the fastest increase in stocks of purchases since January 2023, a business survey showed today. The AIB Ireland Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), compiled by S&P Global, fell to 55.2 in October from 55.5 in September. That was well above the 50 mark that separates growth from contraction. Output growth eased from September's four and a half year high but remained solid, while new orders rose at an accelerated pace that was the second-fastest since April 2022, helped by stronger domestic and overseas sales. Today's reports shows that export orders increased for a ninth consecutive month. Employment also strengthened, with the pace of job creation reaching a three-month high as firms hired to meet demand and expand capacity. Purchasing activity grew at its fastest rate since May, and stocks of purchases rose at the quickest pace since January 2023 as some manufacturers built safety stocks amid shipping delays and tight transport capacity.

stories.title: Kelly hails the 'greatest Loughrea team of all time'
stories.summary: Loughrea senior hurling manager Tommy Kelly has lauded the efforts of his side in claiming a third Galway title on the spin, highlighting a case of the club now doing things the right way. It was a nervy finish though, with Tiernan Killen firing over the winning point against Tommy Larkin's, a club appearing in their first final since their sole success in 1971, at Pearse Stadium on Sunday. Larkin's will have huge regrets about not building a much bigger lead than 0-10 to 0-07 when they were on top in the opening half, not least their failure to put away goal chances. Loughrea never panicked, only taking the lead for the first time 12 minutes from the end and trailing going into stoppage time before Killeen levelled and then landed the winner in a dramatic finish to secure the club's fifth title. Their latest success was always going to be hard won, with Kelly applauding the efforts of Larkin's in getting back to a decider in what Kelly described as a "hard championship" to win. "They last won it in 1971 and there is a great connection between the two clubs. In '71 Loughrea won the minor championship and in 2006 when we the senior Tommy Larkin's won the minor. It's fantastic for east Galway to have them back, to have them at the top table. Their team is made up of big strong lads.

stories.title: Whishaw says Bond franchise 'needs to be reinvented'
stories.summary: Former James Bond actor Ben Whishaw has said he thinks the 007 franchise "needs to be reinvented completely" for its next instalment. The 46-year-old has starred in three James Bond films alongside Daniel Craig as the character of Q, the quartermaster who heads the MI6 research and development team. His first appearance was in the 2012 film Skyfall, and he later featured in Spectre (2015) before reprising his role a final time in Craig's last film as the secret agent, No Time To Die (2021). The hunt for the next Bond began in May and is believed to have reached its final stages, with Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor among the stars reportedly in contention for the 007 role. In an interview with The Sunday Times, Whishaw reflected on the future of the franchise. "The world has changed so much since the last Bond film so you have to find what is relevant about it," he said.

stories.title: Surge in early voting as candidates make final push in US
stories.summary: Candidates across the United States are making their final campaign push today ahead of tomorrow's midterm elections. Both parties are seeking to mobilise supporters and secure votes in a contest that will determine control of Congress. There has been a surge in early voting for the US midterm elections, with more than 54 million people having cast a ballot. Republicans are fighting to defend their control of Congress at a time when affordability is a major concern for voters. Polling suggests Democrats are in a strong position to win a majority in the House of Representatives, but the battle for control of the Senate remains a toss-up. For his closing argument, US President Donald Trump chose a speech in Washington at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool - a landmark that has become synonymous with the 80-year-old's obsessive, controversial drive to redevelop the US capital.

stories.title: Euronext CEO Boujnah to step down
stories.summary: Euronext said today that Stéphane Boujnah, who has led the company since 2015, will step down as chief executive next year, with Dutch company NN Group's CEO David Knibbe set to replace him. In a separate statement, NN Group said Tjeerd Bosklopper would succeed Knibbe as CEO after the insurer's annual general meeting on May 12, 2027. Euronext said it plans to nominate Knibbe at its annual general meeting on May 20, 2027, A spokesperson for Euronext declined to comment beyond the company's statement, citing a quiet period before the publication of its third-quarter results.

stories.title: O'Connor relishing UCD's do-or-die date with Drogheda
stories.summary: After seeing his side overcome Bray Wanderers in the First Division play-off final, UCD manager Willie O'Connor is now looking ahead to a showdown with Drogheda United, believing his side are ready to take their place in League of Ireland Premier Division. At Tolka Park, goals from Sam Norval, Ciarán Behan and Hugh Smith completed a fightback for the Students after Bray had taken the lead against the run of play through Dean O'Shea midway through the first period. UCD will now face Drogs for a pace in the top flight at Tallaght Stadium on Saturday next at 5:30pm. Breaking the game down, he added: "In possession we started the game really, really well, were breaking through the press and created chances. They scored against the run of play and we were disappointed to concede from that corner. "We have the best record in the First Division for and against corners so to concede from that was disappointing. But the reaction from the boys after that to keep playing the way they were playing and to turn the game around and to get in 2-1 at half time tells you a lot about their mindset and character." And while Bray may have had a lot of the ball for periods after the break, O'Connor was happy with his side's shape, saying: "I think we went into the block a little bit too early but we were comfortable enough in it in that we weren't giving up too many chances.

stories.title: Families of Disappeared make fresh appeal for information
stories.summary: A renewed appeal has been made over four men and a woman secretly murdered and buried by paramilitaries in Northern Ireland who remain missing. Joe Lynskey, Columba McVeigh, Robert Nairac, Seamus Maguire and Lisa Dorrian will be remembered at the 20th annual All Souls Silent Walk for the Disappeared at Stormont today. Their families will walk from Carson's Statue to the steps of Parliament Buildings to lay a black wreath, with five white lilies representing those who have yet to be found. Father Joe Gormley will lead prayers, and there will be contributions from family members. It is expected that Rosalie Flanagan, commissioner on the Independent Commission for the Location of Victims' Remains (ICLVR), will attend along with Eamonn Henry, lead investigator of the ICLVR. The ICLVR's search for Mr Maguire continues at Derryclone, near Lurgan.

stories.title: Binance sees outflows stabilising as exchange back online
stories.summary: Binance customers pulled $3.64 billion, or 2.1% of its assets, as the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange resumed service after a security breach linked to North Korea saw $6.3 billion stolen from the platform last week. The exchange moved to reassure crypto investors and said withdrawals were stabilising after an initial spike and deposit volumes had remained "substantial" after, what analysts believe, may be the world's biggest financial robbery ever. After hitting a six-week low on Friday, bitcoin prices recovered slightly through the weekend to trade above $78,000 today. Ether hit a two-month low on Friday and also recovered a little to $2,287. Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally. It said on Sunday it had $171 billion in total assets under management as of October 28. The Binance theft adds to a string of recent crypto thefts. Attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 incidents last year, according to researchers at TRM Labs. Withdrawal levels are an early test of whether customers still trust Binance with their money after the attack. The exchange said it had covered 95% of the assets stolen in the heist.

stories.title: NFL: Broncos pip Chiefs as Vikings' unbeaten run ends
stories.summary: The Denver Broncos' defence stuffed Kansas City on the goal line at the death to beat the Chiefs 28-24. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix led Denver back from a double-digit deficit in the fourth quarter, before defensive tackle Malcolm Roach sacked Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes on the final play of the game. The Los Angeles Rams put together their best performance of the season in a 24-9 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Drake Maye had three touchdowns to lead the New England Patriots past the Miami Dolphins 24-19, while the Philadelphia Eagles coughed up an early lead to go down 27-10 to the Washington Commanders. The Detroit Lions picked up a third successive victory with a closely fought 19-15 victory over the Minnesota Vikings who lost for the first time this season. The Vikings led 7-6 at the break thanks to Justin Jefferson's touchdown but the Lions turned things around in the second half.

stories.title: Empty shopfront proposal part of town centre revival plan
stories.summary: A plan to revive town centres by turning empty shopfronts into new local businesses is being proposed by Minister of State for Retail Alan Dillon. Local authorities, regeneration officers, and Local Enterprise Offices will be asked to match vacant premises with the needs of the community as part of an initiative that will be rolled out in 26 designated towns. The towns are Tullow, Bailieborough, Sixmilebridge, Skibbereen, Milford, Lusk, Gort, Milltown (Co Kerry) Clane, Urlingford, Rathdowney, Carrick-on-Shannon, Abbeyfeale, Longford town, Dunleer, Killala, Enfield, Carrickmacross, Clara, Strokestown, Tubbercurry, Roscrea, Portlaw, Moate, New Ross and Blessington. The proposal aims to boost main street footfall and create sustainable jobs. Business owners will be offered supports, including practical advice, financial mentoring, and marketing assistance. "Empty shopfronts do not create jobs, attract visitors, or support local communities," Mr Dillon said.

stories.summary: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says his side's first Premier League victory at Liverpool in 14 years was inspired by their shock Carabao Cup exit at Fleetwood. But the champions responded in style on Sunday, claiming a hard-fought 1-0 win at Anfield to move top of the Premier League table. Arteta said: "It has been such a long time without having this winning feeling here. "We are extremely proud of the team and the players and what everyone has done, especially in the conditions in which we arrived to this game – the defeat against Fleetwood looks the end of the world, but then you have to pick yourself up. "How the hell can you go out of the cup when you shoot 27 times and have the chances we had against a team who had one shot on target? Then you look so silly but I had the feeling now was the moment.

stories.title: Nine dead as private jet crashes in Florida neighbourhood
stories.summary: A private jet carrying nine people nosedived into a residential neighbourhood in Florida and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy road. Everyone on board was killed, the US transportation secretary said. The crash occurred near Cresthaven, a neighbourhood in Palm Beach County that is less than seven miles (11 kilometres) from President Donald Trump's resort home Mar-a-Lago. The plane came down near the entrance to a mobile home park, Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores said, noting about 600 residents were evacuated and relocated to shelters. Video recorded by people inside their cars captured the moment the aircraft fell from the sky before striking near the road and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crash site as locals expressed shock that it landed only feet from homes and only inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the site.

stories.title: Mulcahy: We're representing Cork - we're disappointed
stories.summary: Glen Rovers manager Tomás Mulcahy admitted his side couldn't live with Clare champions Inagh-Kilnamona as they exited the Munster club championship at the first hurdle. Mulcahy guided the Blackpool side their first Cork Premier Senior Hurling championship in 10 years a fortnight ago but they were always second best against the first-time champions from Clare, going 0-06 to 0-01 behind after 10 minutes, a gap they were never really able to peg back. It's 2009 since the Cork senior champions last added the Munster crown to the Sean Óg Murphy Cup, when the great Newtownshandrum side of the 2000s won their third provincial crown of the decade. Sarsfields did become the first Cork side to win the Munster club SHC in 15 years in 2024 and reached the subsequent All-Ireland final where they lost to Na Fianna. However, the Glanmire club were not Cork champions at the time, having lost that season's county final to East Cork divisional outfit Imokilly. Glen Rovers won the inaugural Munster club championship back in 1964 - prior to the establishment of the All-Ireland series - and two further titles in 1973 and 1977. However, their three recent tilts have been underwhelming. "But you've got to give credit to Inagh-Kilnamona. They came with a gameplan. They dropped a bit deep. They had a man in front of [Eoin] O'Leary. They saw the threat he was in the Cork championship. So it took us a while to adapt to that

stories.title: Iran warns of 'longer' war after Trump threatens strikes
stories.summary: Iran has warned that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of back-and-forth attacks, after President Donald Trump said he still had to "take care" of more targets. Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the US and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections. "A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion," said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television. In the most intense phase of the war, which began on 28 February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran retaliated with missile and drone attacks across the region. Iran-aligned armed groups joined the fighting in Lebanon and Yemen. Mr Akraminia's remarks followed Mr Trump's suggestion that the US could swiftly strike its remaining targets in Iran. stories.title: History made as Antonelli crowned F1 world champion
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli has become the youngest Formula One world champion in history by clinching the title with third place at an action-packed Mexican Grand Prix. Aged just 20 years and 68 days, Antonelli's extraordinary march to the crown in his second season in the sport was completed under the Mexico City sun. He only needed to finish ninth to get over the line but the Italian vowed to finish the job in style. He had to settled for a podium, as he became the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Lewis Hamilton ended a 1,197-day wait for pole on Saturday, pipping George Russell - the Britons the only drivers who could have prevented the coronation had Antonelli failed to score. Max Verstappen claimed a sixth win in Mexico, as he fought off Hamilton at a second race start to clinch a third victory in four races and jump to second in the standings - 119 behind Antonelli. Hamilton was furious after a first-lap scuffle with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc. Antonelli passed Leclerc to finish on the podium, with Lando Norris fifth ahead of Russell.

stories.title: Taliban voices concern over US plans to deport Afghans
stories.summary: Afghanistan's Taliban authorities voiced concern over reported plans by Washington to deport scores of Afghan immigrants to Pakistan with the aim of their eventual return to their home country. More than 150 Afghans in the United States would be deported via Pakistan to Afghanistan, including relatives of those who assisted US forces before their 2021 withdrawal, according to US media reports and an advocacy group. "The Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan expresses its serious concern over reports that the United States intends to deport some Afghan refugees to Pakistan who have not yet been able to obtain legal residency documents in that country," foreign ministry spokesman Abdul Qahar Balkhi said in a statement. Advocacy groups have warned that the removal of former allies and their families could endanger their lives. After regaining power, Taliban authorities announced a general amnesty for Afghans who worked with Western-backed forces and governments and have repeated promises this year that their former foes could safely return home. However, the United Nations has recorded reports of extrajudicial killings, detentions and abuses.

stories.title: Man charged with murder after stabbing at IPAS centre
stories.summary: A 49-year-old man has been charged in connection with an incident in which a man died, and another was injured following a stabbing at an International Protection Accommodation Services centre in Co Kerry. Emergency services were called to the scene at Ballymullen Barracks in Tralee yesterday shortly after 5.20am. Ismail Mustaph Hussan was brought before a special sitting of Killarney District Court this evening. He is charged with the murder of Muhudin Osman Suleyman at Ballymullen Barracks yesterday morning contrary to common law. The Somali national is further charged with Section 3 assault causing harm to another man at the same location. Detective Sergeant James Hurley of Tralee Garda Station gave evidence of arrest, charge and caution.

stories.summary: Ciara Mageean gracefully balanced the qualities of warmth and determination to become one of Ireland's most beloved sports stars of the modern era. Mageean announced herself onto the global stage with world underage medals in 2009 and 2010 and had a career that spanned 16 years culminating with her European title over 1500m in Rome in 2024 but her journey was ultimately cut short. She underwent a second surgery on her achilles in 2024 after withdrawing from the Olympics and was diagnosed with cancer in 2025. Her deep roots in her beloved town of Portaferry on the tip of Ards Peninsula forged an early love with a different sport though. Mageean's sporting talent first shone through on the pitches of Portaferry GAC with a hurl in her hand playing camogie alongside her sisters Máire and Nuala.
